Senses.Explanation: To take a seat and remain sitting. Chan records use the ordinary bodily action in institutionally loaded scenes without making the bare verb itself a separate technical noun. An unnamed monk sits every day in the sutra hall instead of reading scripture. Xuanquan Yan warns clear-eyed patch-robed monks not to 'sit in the mud.' Yuantong Xiu lists three monks in snow—one sitting with his head covered, one sucking a writing brush and composing poetry, and one sitting around the brazier talking about food—and Baichi Yuan calls the first a board-carrying Chan fellow. Hansong Zhicao permits his assembly to sleep or walk and asks why they must rigidly insist on sitting. Wuzu Fayan speaks of Shuangquan sitting amid commotion, while Fachang Yiyu describes eighteen senior men sitting silently around a brazier. The word itself names the seated bodily action; place, duration, posture, institutional setting, and each named speaker's praise or criticism come from the surrounding sentence.
Senses.Note: The corpus has 322 matches in 132 files. 'Sit every day' occurs seven times in seven files; 'sit with the head covered' eighteen times in fifteen; 'sit around a brazier' thirty-five times in twenty-six; and 'sit in the mud' four times in four. The direct nominal form occurs once, in a question about one sitting on Kunlun Mountain. No other required definition formula occurs. The entry therefore uses the plain English action and preserves the corpus's explicit descriptive and critical modifiers rather than introducing a category absent from the Chinese.

Occurrences.Kwic: 昔有一僧。在經堂內不看經。每日打坐。藏主曰。何不看經。僧曰。某甲不識字。主曰。何不問人。僧近前。叉手鞠躬曰。這箇是甚麼字。主無對。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元): an unnamed monk sits every day in the sutra hall without reading scripture, then asks the scripture-store keeper what written character is before him. All six attribution rungs leave the sitting monk unnamed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 山僧今日為諸人說破。明眼衲僧莫去泥裡打坐。珍重。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元): Xuanquan Yan warns clear-eyed patch-robed monks not to go sit in the mud.

Occurrences.Kwic: 復舉圓通秀云：「雪中有三種僧：一者、蒙頭打坐，二者、吮筆吟詩，三者、圍爐說食。」師云：「蒙頭打坐，還他擔板禪和；吮筆吟詩，可是嬌兒賣俏。看來惟圍爐說食底在此時較為親切，何故？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baichi (百癡禪師語錄): Baichi Yuan quotes Yuantong Xiu's list of three monks in snow; Yuantong's quoted words contain the headword, and Baichi follows with his own appraisals.

Occurrences.Kwic: 山僧則不然，青龍今日開爐，親切無如者箇，任從睡臥經行，何必拘拘打坐？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hansong Cao (寒松操禪師語錄): Hansong Zhicao permits his assembly to sleep or walk and asks why they must rigidly insist on sitting.

Occurrences.Kwic: 贏得雙泉，閙中打坐。打坐即不無，且道下水船一曲作麼生唱？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)): Wuzu Fayan says Shuangquan has gained sitting amid commotion, then asks how to sing the tune of a downstream boat.

Occurrences.Kwic: 唯有十八高人緘口圍爐打坐。不是規矩嚴難免見諸人話墮。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continued Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (續傳燈錄): Fachang Yiyu describes eighteen senior men sitting silently around a brazier and says the rules are strict enough to expose their verbal failure.
